purpose: This medication is used every day to help control and prevent asthma symptoms like wheezing, shortness of breath, and chest tightness. It is not a rescue inhaler, so it will not stop an asthma attack that has already started. Using it regularly helps keep your airways calm and reduces swelling so you can breathe more easily day to day.
how_it_works: Beclomethasone is a steroid that works directly in your lungs to reduce inflammation and swelling in your airways. Think of your airways like a tube — when they get irritated and swollen, it is harder to breathe. This medicine helps keep that swelling under control so your airways stay open and relaxed. Because it goes straight to your lungs, very little gets into the rest of your body, making it safer for long-term use than steroid pills.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include a sore or irritated throat, hoarseness or a change in your voice, and a cough. Some people may develop a mouth or throat infection called thrush, which looks like white patches. Rinsing your mouth with water and spitting it out after each use can help prevent these problems.
warnings: Do not use this inhaler during a sudden asthma attack — it will not work fast enough. Always carry a quick-relief rescue inhaler for emergencies. Do not stop using this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better. In children, long-term use may slightly slow growth, so regular check-ups are important. Tell your doctor if you have had any eye problems like glaucoma or cataracts, as this medicine can sometimes affect eye pressure with long-term use.
typical_dosing: Adults and teenagers typically start with 1 to 2 puffs (40 to 80 mcg per puff) inhaled twice a day — once in the morning and once at night. Your doctor may adjust the dose based on how well your asthma is controlled. Children ages 5 and older usually take 1 puff twice a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
